item.title: Young Writers Project: ‘Deep Thoughts’ - VTDigger
item.description: This week’s Young Writers Project entry is “Deep Thoughts” by Teddy Owens, 15, of Essex Junction. Artwork is “Somewhere in the Sky” by Shira Hertzberg, 16, of West Haven.

item.title: Towns ban heavy rigs from muddy roads - VTDigger
item.description: Towns are posting weight restrictions on certain town-owned roads, targeting large trucks and commercial vehicles.

item.title: Matt Swenson: Vermont’s fiscal reckoning is already here - VTDigger
item.description: Vermont keeps buying time. The structural problems keep compounding.

item.title: When Vermont’s treatment landscape shifts, community providers step up - VTDigger
item.description: As Vermont’s substance use treatment landscape shifts, community providers are stepping up to maintain access to care. In Washington County, strong partnerships ensure rapid connection to treatment, recovery services, and coordinated support.

item.title: Brattleboro hospital nurses vote to strike, but delay a date in hopes of spurring talks - VTDigger
item.description: “Our community is at a tipping point,” a union leader said at Brattleboro Memorial Hospital, which is trying to balance a walkout threat and a $14.5 million budget deficit.

item.title: VTDigger Spring Member Drive: Who asks the questions in Montpelier? - VTDigger
item.description: Sometimes VTDigger reporters are the only ones. Your support means we can keep showing up.

item.title: Royalton residents chafe at costs of ongoing Foxstand Bridge closure - VTDigger
item.description: Come April, the Foxstand Bridge will have been closed for two years, and it isn’t slated to reopen until fall of 2028.

item.title: Former Northeast Kingdom Human Services employee sues agency over alleged Medicaid fraud - VTDigger
item.description: The case lands as Congress heightens its scrutiny on Vermont Medicaid waste, fraud and abuse.

item.title: A farmer breeds seeds to withstand Vermont’s unpredictable weather - VTDigger
item.description: Homecoming Seeds offers plants that can germinate in cold soil, withstand fungal diseases, shrug off pests and tolerate temperature swings — while still managing to produce abundantly.
